speaker: ui
en: The Interpreter's House
source: Stage card

speaker: narrator
en: Christian came to the house of the Interpreter, and knocked over and over.
source: Part I: 'he went on till he came at the house of the Interpreter, where he knocked over and over' (verify wording)

speaker: interpreter
en: Come in. I will show you that which will be profitable to you.
source: Part I: 'Come in; I will show thee that which will be profitable to thee' (verify wording)

speaker: sign
en: A large parlour, full of dust, because it was never swept.
source: Part I: 'a very large parlour that was full of dust, because never swept' (verify wording)

speaker: narrator
en: He began to sweep, and the dust flew about so that it almost choked him.
source: Part I: 'the dust began so abundantly to fly about, that Christian had almost therewith been choked' (verify wording)

speaker: damsel
en: Bring water, and sprinkle the room.
source: Part I: 'Bring hither the water, and sprinkle the room' (verify wording)

speaker: narrator
en: Christian took up the jug of water.
source: Adaptation (puzzle step)

speaker: narrator
en: The water laid the dust, and the room was swept and cleansed with pleasure.
source: Part I: 'it was swept and cleansed with pleasure' (verify wording)

speaker: christian
en: The dust is too thick. I need something to settle it.
source: Adaptation (puzzle hint)

speaker: interpreter
en: The dust is sin. The broom is the Law, which only stirs it up. The water is the Gospel, which lays it down.
source: Part I: the Interpreter's explanation of the parlour (paraphrase)

speaker: sign
en: One stands by the fire, always casting water on it, yet the fire burns higher and hotter.
source: Part I: the fire against the wall (paraphrase; verify)

speaker: narrator
en: Behind the wall stood a man with a vessel of oil, secretly casting it into the fire.
source: Part I: 'a man with a vessel of oil in his hand, of the which he did also continually cast, but secretly, into the fire' (verify wording)

speaker: interpreter
en: This is Christ, who with the oil of his grace keeps alive the work already begun in the heart.
source: Part I: 'This is Christ, who continually, with the oil of his grace, maintains the work already begun in the heart' (verify wording)

speaker: sign
en: Salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks.
source: Isaiah 26:1 (KJV), quoted in Part I

speaker: narrator
en: Up this way ran Christian, but not without great difficulty, because of the load on his back.
source: Part I (verify wording)

speaker: narrator
en: Just as Christian came up to the Cross, his burden loosed from his shoulders and fell from his back. It tumbled till it came to the mouth of the sepulchre, where it fell in, and was seen no more.
source: Part I: the burden falls at the Cross (verify wording)

speaker: christian
en: He has given me rest by his sorrow, and life by his death.
source: Part I: 'He hath given me rest by his sorrow, and life by his death' (verify wording)

speaker: shining_one
en: Your sins are forgiven.
source: Part I: the first Shining One, 'Thy sins be forgiven thee' (Mark 2:5)

speaker: shining_one
en: Put off your rags. Here is a change of clothes.
source: Part I: the second Shining One 'stripped him of his rags, and clothed him with change of raiment' (paraphrase)

speaker: shining_one
en: Take this Roll with its seal. Look on it as you run, and give it in at the Celestial Gate.
source: Part I: the third Shining One gives him a roll with a seal (paraphrase; verify)

speaker: narrator
en: Then Christian gave three leaps for joy, and went on singing.
source: Part I: 'Then Christian gave three leaps for joy, and went on singing' (verify wording)

speaker: sign
en: Free of the burden, you can jump again in the air.
source: Mechanic hint (double jump)
